sources.entry: PrivateBin - Minimalist pastebin/discussion board where the server has zero knowledge of hosted data. (Demo, Source Code) Zlib PHP

summary.one_liner: PrivateBin is a minimalist, open source pastebin where data is encrypted in the browser so the server has zero knowledge of stored content.
summary.what_it_does: PrivateBin encrypts and decrypts paste data in the browser using 256-bit AES in Galois Counter mode, so the server only stores ciphertext. Pastes can be protected with a password that is required to read them. The README lists optional features that can be toggled in the configuration file: discussions with nicknames or IP-based identicons, expiration times including "forever" and "burn after reading", Markdown support with preview, syntax highlighting via prettify.js, and file upload with image, media and PDF preview (disabled by default). It also includes templates (bootstrap5, bootstrap CSS, darkstrap), a translation system with browser language detection, and QR codes for paste URLs. It is a fork of ZeroBin that was refactored for easier extensions.
use_cases: send a temporary text note that self-destructs after reading
host an internal encrypted pastebin for a team
discuss a paste with comments in a zero-knowledge setting
share files or images with expiring links
notable: Zero-knowledge design: encryption and decryption happen in the browser, and the key sits in the URL fragment after the #
Fork of ZeroBin refactored for easier extensions
caveats: Must be served over HTTPS, and the server admin must be trusted not to inject malicious code
Anyone with the URL can read a paste that is not password-protected
Access logs may still reveal who accessed a paste
